newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end down in quiet pre-tankan trade.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end down in quiet pre-tankan trade.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract ended lower on Friday due to long liquidation by dealers, traders said.
JGB market sentiment was weakened by the dollar's rise against the yen in Tokyo trade, they said.

"Earlier there had been speculation that the dollar may fall against the yen ahead of the Group of Seven (G7) summit, and when the dollar rose today contrary to such expectations selling of JGBs ensued," a trust bank trader said.
The September ended at 123.87, down from Thursday's close of 124.06. Turnover was 26,800 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.400 percent as of 0647 GMT, up from Thursday's close of 2.385 percent.
JGBs carried over weakness from late on Thursday and from LIFFE overnight, traders said.
"JGBs were repelled and flung off highs after trying for the upside on Thursday, and that contributed to today's decline," the trust bank trader said.

Traders said JGBs were sold on LIFFE on Thursday after Toyoo Gyohten, a former senior official of Japan's Finance Ministry, said August could be the earliest date that Japan could consider changing its monetary policy.
The only surprise on Friday was the extent of the September's fall at the open, traders said.
"It was a bit surprising that the September opened so low. There was no significant reason for the fall... It is not as if investors were selling early in the morning," the first trader said.
The September opened at 123.76, the intra-day low on Friday. The day's high was 123.95.
JGBs were lifted off early lows, partly due to cash JGBs buying on dips by investors, a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
Trade was generally subdued as market players adopted a cautious stance ahead of release of the Bank of Japan's key "tankan" corporate sentiment survey next Wednesday, traders said.
Concern over a 10-year JGB auction which is expected to take place next Tuesday is also casting a pall over the market, traders said.

Reluctance on the part of investors to buy ahead of the long-awaited tankan as well as the suspension of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd and Nomura Securities Co Ltd from JGB auctions and underwriting may lead to poor auction results, they said.
